title: HSM onprem integration and cross-border key policy review - Sigma Banking
summary: Customer checking feasibility of on-prem HSM / BYOK for Redwood Private; primary concerns are cross-border key residency, remote attestation, audit log fidelity, and DR/key-recovery procedures. Discussed envelope encryption, key wrapping, periodic rotation, and integration patterns with CloudHSM / Thales / customer HSM appliance.
topics: Audit logs and KMS audit trail fidelity
action_items: Marta Ruiz: Share Sigma's internal HSM vendor spec sheet and network diagram by 2025-11-19
Priya Desai (Redwood): Draft a step-by-step BYOK import runbook and sample CLI commands by 2025-11-21
Jon Park (Redwood): Provide remote attestation acceptance criteria and supported HSM firmware versions by 2025-11-20
next_steps: Redwood to send HSM integration checklist and a short demo video of BYOK import
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive with on-prem infra team (prefer week of 11/24)
Customer to confirm legal/regulatory key residency constraints for EU/UK vs APAC
transcript_text:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-14
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 54 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jon Park (Redwood Product Security), Marta Ruiz (Sigma Head Cloud Security), Ethan Cole (Sigma Platform Eng), Ramesh Iyer (Sigma Compliance)

Summary (auto): quick security review focused on KMS/BYOK/HSM for Redwood Private; practical integration steps and policy constraints.

[00:00:00] Alex Moreno: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick run through on the HSM and BYOK flow for Redwood Private. we have priya on the line to go through the technical pieces and jon for attestation and audit requirements. Marta, do you want to kick off with the high level ask?

[00:00:28] Marta Ruiz: sure, thanks alex. from sigma's perspective we need to ensure any keys used to encrypt customer data remain in-scope for EU residency. so two asks: one, we want to import customer-managed keys into our on-prem HSM but still use Redwood Private for inference. two, we need the attestation evidence and full audit logs — like key usage, wrap/unwrap ops, and which node (or region) had access.

[00:00:55] Priya Desai: okay good. high level, there are two patterns we usually recommend: envelope encryption where Redwood stores ciphertext and only the key-encrypting-key (KEK) lives in the customer's HSM, or a strictly proxy model where the HSM is called for every token operation. the envelope pattern gives better latency and throughput because data keys are cached, but then you need to think about prefix caching and cache TTLs.

[00:01:22] Ethan Cole: caching TTLs — that is the tricky bit for us. our compliance team is nervous about any in-memory keying material on vendor infrastructure even for short TTLs. is there a middle ground?

[00:01:41] Jon Park: yeah that's common. you can adopt an approach where data keys are ephemeral and wrapped with the HSM KEK, but you set very aggressive TTLs and require hardware-backed key unwrapping for every rehydrate beyond X seconds. also we support remote attestation so you can verify the runtime before allowing any unwraps.

[00:02:05] Ramesh Iyer: on remote attestation — are we talking TPM-based attestation, HSM attest, or something like a signed cert from the device? we need formal evidence for audits.

[00:02:21] Jon Park: good question. Redwood supports HSM vendor-signed attestation tokens (e.g., Thales/Entrust-style), and for cloud HSMs we accept CloudHSM signed cert chains. the artifact we provide is a timestamped attestation + the public key fingerprint of the KEK. we can export that into the audit bundle. small caveat: the attestation format differs by vendor so we'd show the mapping in the runbook.

[00:02:48] Alex Moreno: fwiw we also have a policy doc that maps attestation fields to compliance requirements — link in chat: https://redwood.internal/docs/security/hsm-attestation (note: internal link for SEC+compliance).

[00:03:10] Marta Ruiz: perfect. another constraint: cross-border. Sigma must not move EU keys to APAC. so even if Redwood has multi-region infra, the KEKs must not leave eu-west-1. can we lock a KEK to a region and disable replication?

[00:03:29] Priya Desai: yes, customers can pin KEKs to a region. in Redwood Private when you configure BYOK you select the key-residency policy: single-region, per-account-region, or global. we can set it to single-region and disable automated replication. note though — disaster recovery becomes more manual; we typically propose an escrow flow for DR where a sealed copy of the wrapped key is stored in a second-region HSM under customer control with strict legal approval.

[00:03:58] Ethan Cole: the escrow idea — that might be workable if it's manual and audited. what about key rotation? do you support automatic rotation of KEKs in a BYOK setup?

[00:04:13] Priya Desai: rotation is supported, yes. we do rolling rotation where the new KEK is imported and then we rewrap active data keys over time. rotation has two dimensions: KEK rotation and data-key rotation. with BYOK you as the customer can trigger KEK rotation from your HSM and then we initiate rewraps; or we can perform scheduled rotation with your approval. logging captures every wrap/unwrap event.

[00:04:37] Ramesh Iyer: logging fidelity — can logs show node identifiers, call stacks, and the exact API call payload? our auditors want request IDs tied to user identity and SAML principals.

[00:04:55] Jon Park: yes, our audit trail includes timestamp, request id, redwood-service-instance id (a short hash), operation (wrap/unwrap/import/export), principal (mapped to SAML subject), and the HSM attestation snapshot. payloads are redacted for PII but we can keep request headers and metadata. we can also forward logs to your SIEM via syslog/S3 push with retention controls.

[00:05:20] Marta Ruiz: retention controls — what are the retention limits? we need 7 years for some transactions per banking regs.

[00:05:30] Alex Moreno: by default Redwood Console retains key operation logs for 90 days, enterprise customers can request extended retention up to 7 years as a paid add-on; for Private deployments we can configure long-term archival to your S3 or on-prem storage. there may be export size and cost considerations.

[00:05:48] Ethan Cole: what about RBAC for key ops — can we restrict who in Sigma does wrap/unwrap or import? we don't want devs to be able to import keys.

[00:06:03] Priya Desai: absolutely. RBAC maps to SSO Roles via SAML/SCIM. we support role-based policies like key-admin, key-operator, key-viewer. key-admin can import/export and set policies, key-operator can request unwraps for runtime operations but cannot export private key material. we also have MFA gating for export operations and step-up auth for high-sensitivity API calls.

[00:06:26] Ramesh Iyer: step-up auth — is that integrated with our IdP? we use Okta with custom policies.

[00:06:34] Jon Park: yes, we integrate with Okta, Azure AD, anything supporting SAML + OIDC. step-up is implemented via an extra SAML assertion that indicates a policy step-up was performed; we map that to a short-lived elevated token in Redwood.

[00:06:50] Marta Ruiz: network topology question — if we run Redwood Private inside our VPC, do key unwrap calls from Redwood nodes go over the public internet to the HSM, or can we use direct private peering?

[00:07:06] Priya Desai: you can do private connectivity. for on-prem HSM appliances behind your firewall we recommend a private tunnel (IPsec/Direct Connect equivalent) and strict source-IP allowlists for HSM management ports. for cloud-based HSMs we typically use VPC endpoints and private peering. we avoid public egress for any key material operations.

[00:07:29] Ethan Cole: great. a detail on HSM models — which HSMs have you validated? our procurement uses Thales nShield and one of the older SafeNet models.

[00:07:40] Jon Park: we've validated Thales nShield, AWS CloudHSM, Azure KeyVault HSM, and a range of PKCS#11-compatible appliances including SafeNet. for older firmware versions we might need a patch; we keep a compatibility matrix. i'll attach the matrix after the call.

[00:07:56] Alex Moreno: noted — jon will share the compatibility matrix. link to our BYOK runbook: https://redwood.tools/byok-runbook (shared doc).

[00:08:15] Marta Ruiz: there's also procurement: chain of custody for key import. we probably want to use a hardware token to import the initial root KEK to the HSM. do you support offline key import ceremonies?

[00:08:29] Priya Desai: yes, we support offline import ceremonies. typical flow: customer generates KEK in HSM, exports public-wrapped form or a wrapped blob to Redwood, we perform a verification handshake, and then we store only the wrapped KEK. we do not possess unwrapped key material. for the initial proofing we can do a KMS import manifest and notarize the hash via signed attestation.

[00:08:54] Marta Ruiz: notarization — do you use an internal CA or do you accept third-party notarization?

[00:09:01] Jon Park: we accept third-party notarization; many banks prefer a neutral auditor to witness the ceremony. we can generate a manifest that the auditor signs.

[00:09:11] Ethan Cole: what about operational performance — if every unwrap goes to the HSM, it could add latency. for low-latency inference we need unwraps to be fast, how do you reconcile that?

[00:09:25] Priya Desai: that's the tradeoff. full-proxy unwraps incur HSM RTT on each call — typically 10s-100s ms depending on topology. envelope with ephemeral data keys reduces calls to HSM to a cache miss only. many customers use aggressive TTLs with enhanced attestation to balance risk. also we support local hardware accelerators and batching for unwraps where possible.

[00:09:49] Marta Ruiz: can Redwood's runtime be deployed inside our data center to avoid network latency?

[00:09:57] Alex Moreno: yes, Redwood Private is installable in-customer VPC or air-gapped on-prem. that way the runtime is local to your HSM. we've done on-prem installs for other banks. provisioning is done via our private operator image and config; we'll need an infra runbook.

[00:10:12] Ramesh Iyer: for air-gapped installs, how do updates and attestation work? we can't have outbound connectivity for runtime attestation checks.

[00:10:23] Jon Park: for air-gapped, attestation uses an offline signed bundle approach. you run our attestation collector which signs the runtime fingerprint with your on-prem key and then an offline auditor or Redwood support ingests that signed bundle during scheduled maintenance windows. patching is manual via signed images we provide on a secure media.

[00:10:45] Marta Ruiz: okay that helps. one more thing — key compromise and rotation emergency. what's the recovery policy if a KEK is suspected compromised?

[00:10:56] Priya Desai: the emergency flow: 1) freeze key (mark as revoked), 2) rotate to a new KEK and rewrap, 3) ephemeral sessions are invalidated and nodes request new data keys, 4) we provide an audit package and forensics export. the timeline depends on data volume for rewraps. we can also assist with an emergency key-escrow-to-cold-hsm option if you require a secondary keyholder.

[00:11:24] Ethan Cole: assistance during incident — do you have a runbook and SLA for on-call security support?

[00:11:31] Alex Moreno: enterprise customers get a 24/7 security on-call rotation plus a runbook. that's included for Dedicated/Private under the enterprise support tier. we'll share an incident response annex.

[00:11:44] Ramesh Iyer: auditability question again: can we get raw HSM logs or only a normalized export? some auditors want HSM vendor logs for deep forensics.

[00:11:55] Jon Park: we can export raw HSM vendor logs as part of a support engagement; however that typically requires an NDA and support-level agreement because vendor logs contain sensitive firmware-level details. for day-to-day purposes we provide a normalized, queryable audit export.

[00:12:15] Marta Ruiz: okay, procurement will need estimated costs for long-term log retention and the escrow key storage.

[00:12:24] Alex Moreno: we'll include cost guidance in the follow-up email.

[00:12:30] Ethan Cole: question about key wrapping algorithms — do you support AES-GCM wrapping or only RSA-OAEP style? our HSM only exports symmetric KEKs.

[00:12:43] Priya Desai: we support AES-KW, AES-GCM, and RSA-OAEP depending on vendor. our platform is PKCS#11-aware and can accept wrapped blobs under a variety of algorithms; we'll note exact acceptable ciphers in the runbook.

[00:13:00] Marta Ruiz: are there any compliance gaps you see with our current ask? we described: BYOK, single-region pinned KEK, offline import ceremony, seven-year audit retention, and restricted RBAC.

[00:13:11] Jon Park: nothing fundamental blocks that. the main gaps are operational: 1) define DR escrow policy and legal approvals, 2) map IdP roles to Redwood RBAC and verify step-up config, 3) confirm network topology to ensure no public egress for unwrap calls. all are resolvable and we'll provide templates.

[00:13:33] Marta Ruiz: great. small nit: ''KV cache'' in your docs — we assume you mean runtime key cache not key-value store? sometimes the term confuses auditors.

[00:13:43] Alex Moreno: yes, runtime key cache. we'll clarify language to say "data-key cache (ephemeral)". good catch.

[00:13:52] Ethan Cole: any known gotchas from previous bank integrations?

[00:13:57] Priya Desai: a few: mismatched PKCS#11 drivers causing unwrap failures, time-skew between HSM and runtime impacting attestations, and network MTU issues on tunneled paths causing large blob failures. we include test scripts to validate those.

[00:14:17] Ramesh Iyer: test scripts — can we run them in our staging environment? would need a spared HSM slot or CloudHSM instance.

[00:14:26] Jon Park: yes, we typically provision a CloudHSM test cluster for staging or use a virtual HSM simulator for initial validation. real HSM testing is recommended prior to production.

[00:14:37] Marta Ruiz: next steps recap?

[00:14:40] Alex Moreno: sure. priya and jon will share the compatibility matrix, BYOK runbook link, and an attestation sample bundle. marta will share Sigma's HSM specs and legal/regulatory constraints. redwood to prepare a short cost estimate for long-term log retention and escrow storage. propose follow-up deep-dive with infra in week of 11/24.

[00:15:02] Ethan Cole: sounds good. thanks everyone.

[00:15:05] Alex Moreno: thanks all. I'll send notes and links. bye.

End of call.

Notes on transcription: rustle of papers heard at 00:08:15; occasional crosstalk at 00:09:49. Some vendor names transcribed imperfectly (SafeNet sometimes as "safe-net").
